Attribute conversions to channels under several rules at once

Source: R/attribute.R
attribute.Rd

Runs a set of credit rules over the same journey table and returns their results stacked, so the spread between rules is visible rather than hidden by a choice of default. That spread is the most useful output of rule-based attribution: it bounds how much a channel's apparent value depends on the convention rather than the data.

Usage

attribute(
  paths,
  rules = c("linear", "first", "last", "position", "time_decay", "markov"),
  first_weight = 0.4,
  last_weight = 0.4,
  decay = decay_from_half_life(7),
  period = 1,
  by = NULL,
  times = 0L,
  level = 0.9,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

paths

An mm_paths object from build_paths().

rules

Character vector of rules to apply: any of "linear", "first", "last", "position", "time_decay" and "markov". The first five are heuristic conventions; "markov" is the data-driven removal-effect model of markov_removal(). All six are run by default. A rule named twice is run once.

first_weight, last_weight

Passed to credit_position().

decay, period

Passed to credit_time_decay().

by

Optional names of columns of paths that divide the journeys into segments, such as a device column carried by the keep argument of build_paths(). Every rule then runs on each segment's journeys alone, so shares sum to 1 within each segment and rule (or are all 0 in a segment with no conversions), and the Markov chain is fitted per segment. Each column must take one value per journey and have no missing values. See Segments.

times

Number of bootstrap replicates behind intervals on the shares: 0, the default, for no intervals, or from 2 to 1,000,000. See Intervals.

level

Confidence level of the percentile intervals, in (0, 1).

seed

Optional random seed, one whole number, for reproducible intervals. The caller's random number stream is restored afterwards. Giving level or seed with times = 0 has no effect, and a warning says so.

Value

A data frame with one row per rule and channel, or per segment, rule and channel when by is given:

The by columns

The segment, in the columns' own types. Present only with by.

rule

Which credit rule produced the row.

channel

Channel label.

conversions

Fractional conversions credited to the channel.

share

conversions as a share of all conversions credited under that rule. Shares sum to 1 within each rule, and within each segment; where there is no conversion to share, every share is 0.

lower, upper

Percentile interval for share at level, present only when times is above 0. NA where fewer than two replicates define the share, as in a segment with no converting journey.

value

Credited conversion value, present only when the journey table carries values.

touches

Number of touchpoints on the channel across all journeys, converting or not.

Rows are ordered by segment, then by rule in the order of rules, then by descending conversions, with ties in channel order (C locale, so the same on every platform). Segments are sorted by their values, factors in level order.

The result has class mm_attribution. With by it also has class mm_attribution_segments and the attribute "segments", naming the segment columns. With intervals it also has class mm_attribution_intervals and the attributes "level" and "times". For these two classes plot() draws each rule's share per channel; see plot.mm_attribution_intervals().

Segments

A segment holds whole journeys, so a column given to by must take one value in each journey. A device column kept per touch can change within a cross-device journey; give each journey one value first, for example the device of its last touch:

last <- paths$touch_rank == paths$touch_n
at_last <- match(paths$path_id, paths$path_id[last])
paths$journey_device <- paths$device[last][at_last]

Each segment is attributed as if it were the whole table: a channel's share is its share of that segment's credited conversions, touches counts that segment's touches, and a channel appears only in segments where it has a touch. With the "markov" rule, one warning names every segment with no non-converting journeys, as markov_removal() warns about a whole table without them.

Intervals

With times above 0, the journeys of each segment are resampled with replacement times times, every rule is recomputed on each resample, and lower and upper are percentile intervals of the resampled shares. They show how far the shares move with the sample of journeys observed, with the journey table's construction and each rule held fixed. They say nothing about the choice of rule, which attribution_spread() measures.

A resample gives the same shares as attribute() on a journey table holding the drawn journeys, each draw a separate journey: a heuristic rule credits each journey on its own, so its resampled totals reuse the credit every journey received on the full data, and the Markov chain is refitted from the transitions of the drawn journeys. Journeys are drawn independently, so a customer's several journeys are treated as unrelated. A resample with no converting journey defines no share; it is left out of the intervals and counted in a message.

Every draw comes after seed is set, and the caller's random number stream is restored afterwards, as in block_bootstrap(). Without seed the draws advance the session's stream.

See also

credit_linear() and friends, markov_removal(), attribution_spread(), plot.mm_attribution(), plot.mm_attribution_intervals()

Examples

data(mm_events)
paths <- build_paths(mm_events, id = "customer_id", channel = "channel",
                     timestamp = "timestamp", conversion = "conversion",
                     value = "value")

res <- attribute(paths)
head(res, 10)
#>      rule        channel conversions      share     value touches
#> 1  linear    paid_search   494.40675 0.18037459 63269.896    3203
#> 2  linear        display   482.35595 0.17597809 60241.653    3011
#> 3  linear         social   460.37460 0.16795863 59182.995    2818
#> 4  linear organic_search   425.06786 0.15507766 51503.251    2741
#> 5  linear          email   329.57579 0.12023925 42200.946    2178
#> 6  linear      affiliate   265.93214 0.09702012 33558.401    1734
#> 7  linear        (blank)    91.17024 0.03326167 11382.201     465
#> 8  linear         (none)    81.73690 0.02982010  9640.961     427
#> 9  linear         direct    66.63452 0.02431030  7771.148     444
#> 10 linear      (missing)    43.74524 0.01595959  5951.438     261

# Total credited conversions equals observed converting journeys, per rule
tapply(res$conversions, res$rule, sum)
#>      first       last     linear     markov   position time_decay 
#>       2741       2741       2741       2741       2741       2741 

# How much does the answer depend on the rule?
attribution_spread(res)
#>           channel  min_share  max_share mean_share       spread
#> 1         display 0.07187158 0.29113462 0.17382396 0.2192630427
#> 2     paid_search 0.09157242 0.27252827 0.18342704 0.1809558555
#> 3           email 0.05654870 0.18314484 0.12349952 0.1265961328
#> 4          social 0.11638088 0.22072236 0.16553747 0.1043414812
#> 5  organic_search 0.12623130 0.17876687 0.15470603 0.0525355710
#> 6       affiliate 0.08062751 0.11711054 0.09861140 0.0364830354
#> 7          direct 0.02225465 0.02682848 0.02410676 0.0045738324
#> 8         (blank) 0.02955126 0.03378661 0.03175589 0.0042353471
#> 9          (none) 0.02736228 0.02982010 0.02849282 0.0024578273
#> 10      (missing) 0.01568771 0.01637007 0.01603912 0.0006823617
#>    first_last_ratio
#> 1         4.0507614
#> 2         0.3360107
#> 3         0.3087649
#> 4         1.8965517
#> 5         0.7061224
#> 6         1.4524887
#> 7         1.0491803
#> 8         0.9418605
#> 9         1.0133333
#> 10        1.0232558

# How much does it depend on the sample? 90% intervals from 50 resamples
boot <- attribute(paths, rules = c("first", "last", "markov"), times = 50,
                  seed = 1)
head(boot)
#>    rule        channel conversions      share      lower      upper     value
#> 1 first        display         798 0.29113462 0.27584561 0.30603943 100719.02
#> 2 first         social         605 0.22072236 0.20889362 0.23312958  78372.54
#> 3 first organic_search         346 0.12623130 0.11601449 0.13602582  41455.44
#> 4 first      affiliate         321 0.11711054 0.10586710 0.12843015  40943.15
#> 5 first    paid_search         251 0.09157242 0.08385965 0.09976528  30259.63
#> 6 first          email         155 0.05654870 0.05136549 0.06496043  20063.21
#>   touches
#> 1    3011
#> 2    2818
#> 3    2741
#> 4    1734
#> 5    3203
#> 6    2178

# Credit per segment, here a device recorded once per customer
ev <- mm_events
ev$device <- ifelse(grepl("[02468]$", ev$customer_id), "mobile", "desktop")
kept <- build_paths(ev, id = "customer_id", channel = "channel",
                    timestamp = "timestamp", conversion = "conversion",
                    keep = "device")
by_device <- attribute(kept, rules = c("first", "last"), by = "device")
by_device[by_device$channel == "display", ]
#>     device  rule channel conversions      share touches
#> 1  desktop first display         376 0.27769572    1506
#> 16 desktop  last display         100 0.07385524    1506
#> 21  mobile first display         422 0.30425379    1505
#> 36  mobile  last display          97 0.06993511    1505
